sections.html:
Your municipality mails the Racine County bill and takes the first payment, and the county treasurer picks up from there. Notices go out in December. Outside the City of Racine you may split the bill into two installments, January 31 and July 31, with the first one paid locally.

You will find the county treasurer on the courthouse's 1st floor, north end, at 730 Wisconsin Avenue, open weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:30 pm. The phone is (262) 636-3239 and the email is rctreasurer@racinecounty.gov. A county directory lists the clerk or treasurer for each of the Towns of Burlington, Dover, Norway and Waterford, the Villages of Caledonia, Elmwood Park, Mount Pleasant, North Bay, Raymond, Rochester, Sturtevant, Union Grove, Waterford, Wind Point and Yorkville, and the Cities of Burlington and Racine.

sections.h2: Racine County for a home seller
sections.html: Racine County is a Lake Michigan county of about 198,919 people (2025 estimate), and 67.7 percent of occupied homes are owned by the people living in them. Lakeshore city streets, suburban villages and farm towns all sit inside one border. That means neighbors a few miles apart may pay on different schedules and answer to different assessors. Confirm your municipality first, then quote dates to a buyer.

A sale touches the assessor, a treasurer, the Register of Deeds and the Board of Review clerk. County-level contacts are below.

Racine County offices and payment sites
OfficeAddress and hoursPhone or email
Racine County Treasurer730 Wisconsin Ave, Racine; 8:00 am to 4:30 pm weekdays(262) 636-3239
Racine County Register of Deeds730 Wisconsin Ave, Racine; 8:00 am to 4:30 pm weekdays(262) 636-3208, rod@racinecounty.gov
City of Racine tax paymentsCity Hall, 730 Washington Ave(262) 636-9171
Burlington drop-off for county paymentsBurlington City Hall, 300 N Pine StRacine County Treasurer, (262) 636-3239

The county treasurer accepts payment four ways: at the window, in the courthouse drop box, by mail, or online. Cash, checks and money orders work at the window. Leave only checks in the drop box on the east side facing Wisconsin Avenue, because cash is not accepted there. Mail checks to Racine County Treasurer, 730 Wisconsin Ave, Racine, WI 53403-1274.

  • Card or e-check: dial (800) 272-9829 or pay at OfficialPayments.com with jurisdiction code 5835. Third-party fees apply.
  • Record search: the Ascent Land Records site displays your tax record, and paying there takes the 15-digit parcel ID or tax key number.
  • Alerts: text and email notices can be set up for a parcel.

Brochures on paying real estate taxes, taxpayer help and tax foreclosure sit on the treasurer's pages, along with a glossary and a short guide to pulling your payment history.

Pay late or pay too little and the whole remaining balance comes due immediately. Charges begin February 1: 1 percent interest and a 0.5 percent penalty each month, or 1.5 percent combined (Wis. Stat. s. 74.47). The treasurer cannot waive them.

There is a small grace period. Section 74.11(7) treats the first installment as delinquent only after five working days past January 31 go by unpaid. The county still counts interest from February 1 once you miss, so aim for January 31 itself.

Owners already behind are urged to set up regular payments, and the office takes monthly payments on delinquent bills. Get a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

Racine County takes properties through tax foreclosure and then sells them at public sales run by the County Treasurer. There are three kinds: sealed bid, subsequent sealed bid and over-the-counter. You can join a buyers' email list for sale notices, and the Sheriff's Sale site covers sheriff's sales separately.

A Tax Foreclosure FAQ brochure is available from the treasurer. If several years are unpaid and you want to sell, closing before foreclosure begins gives you the most room. Ask which years are open and what clears them.

A disagreement over value is settled at your municipality's Board of Review, not at the treasurer's counter. Every town, village and city has its own board, and its clerk must post notice 15 days ahead of the first session (30 days in a revaluation year). Call the clerk each spring for dates.

  • Give the clerk written or oral notice 48 hours before the first meeting, or show good cause in the meeting's first two hours.
  • Hand in a written objection during those same two hours.
  • Challenge the combined land and building value, since s. 70.47(7)(a) rules out objecting to only one part.
  • Plan to be sworn in. Owners and their witnesses are heard first.

sections.h2: Tax credits that lower a bill
sections.html:
Two credits are worth checking. A lottery and gaming credit cuts the bill on a qualifying home, managed through the state revenue department's online portal, where late claims are due by October 1.

The homestead credit works differently: it is filed with your Wisconsin income tax return and helps lower-income households with property tax or rent. A fact sheet linked from the county explains eligibility, and a veteran's credit page is linked too.

sections.h2: Recording a deed at the Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Documents reach the Register of Deeds, also at 730 Wisconsin Avenue, by drop-off, mail or e-filing. Sellers who skip e-filing are told to go through a title company or an e-recording service provider. Self-serve search computers run 8:30 am to 4:00 pm and staff cannot run searches for you.

Costs are fixed by statute: $30 to record (s. 59.43(2)(ag)), plus a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value (s. 77.22). Passing property by will or survivorship carries no fee, and some family transfers for token consideration are exempt as well.

Take it in this order.

  1. Look up the parcel and list the unpaid years.
  2. Ask whichever treasurer holds your installments for a full payoff, interest included.
  3. Pass the number to the title company so it is paid from your proceeds.
  4. File the transfer return and record the deed.

The calendar depends on location. City of Racine homes have four installments, while Mount Pleasant and Caledonia homes have two. From August 1 onward everything, city parcels included, is paid to the county.

A cash buyer or a financed buyer will both need the payoff, deed and transfer return. Compare every figure with the county tax record before you say yes to an offer.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Racine County property taxes?
faqs.a: First installments go to your local municipality. Second installments and back taxes go to the county treasurer at 730 Wisconsin Avenue. The City of Racine takes its own four installments through July 31.

faqs.q: What is the Racine County treasurer's phone number?
faqs.a: It is (262) 636-3239. Walk-in hours at the courthouse, 730 Wisconsin Avenue, are weekdays 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: What interest do late taxes carry in Racine County?
faqs.a: Each month adds 1 percent interest and a 0.5 percent penalty, 1.5 percent in all. The county has no authority to forgive it.

faqs.q: Can I pay Racine County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Call (800) 272-9829 or use OfficialPayments.com with jurisdiction code 5835. Third-party fees apply, and the drop box does not accept cash.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Racine County?
faqs.a: The recording charge is $30, and the transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 of value unless an exemption applies. The Register of Deeds can confirm at (262) 636-3208.
